newsitem.title: MEXICO: Troops to replace cops temporarily in Mexico City.
newsitem.headline: Troops to replace cops temporarily in Mexico City.

text.p: Nearly 3,000 soldiers will temporarily replace civilian police in Mexico's capital as part of a long-term programme to root out corruption and inefficiency, officials said on Friday.

Mexican police officials said that for the next 32 months, military police will take over civilian functions in two-month rotations around Mexico City, while police officers attend weapons, ethics and other training courses run by the army.
The move is the latest evidence of the military's growing role in Mexico's notoriously corrupt police force. However, the stand-in law enforcers will wear regular police uniforms, not military dress.

The move was proposed on Thursday by Mexico City Chief of Police Enrique Salgado, himself an army general, to local legislators. It had already been approved by President Ernesto Zedillo, legislators said.

Pedro Penaloza, the head of the Security Commission in Mexico City's Legislative Assembly, described the civilian police force in a radio interview on Friday as a "Frankenstein" that was facing a "historic crisis."
Even though police receive training upon joining the force, they are corrupted by their superiors as soon as they begin active duty, Penaloza said.
Such practices included bribing their superior officers for the right to extort civilians or motorists at strategic points around the city, he said.
Mexico City residents had widely called for a growing military role in security amid a huge crime wave after Mexico plunged into economic crisis in December 1994.

But the army's image as crime fighter was tainted in February by the arrest of the head of the country's anti-drugs police, Gen. Jesus Gutierrez Rebollo, the first military official to have held such a post.
